a01: Outside this city, Stephen fell under the stones. I will never forget that day as long as I live.
As the stones flew, he knelt down and prayed for the very people who were stoning him.
I thought his death was right. Back then, I did.
a02: Carrying letters from the high priest, I walked this road to arrest the followers of Jesus.
As I came near Damascus, a light brighter than the noonday sun flashed around me.
Lying on the ground, I heard His voice for the first time.
a03: Blind, I was led into this city by the hand.
A disciple who had been afraid of me heard the Lord's word and knocked on the door of the house where I was staying.
When he laid his hands on me, something like scales fell from my eyes.
a04: When I preached Jesus in this city, this time I was the one being hunted.
Day and night, men stood watch at every city gate to catch me.
On a pitch-dark night, I slipped out of this city without anyone knowing.
a05: I came back to Jerusalem, but the disciples were all afraid of me.
Then one man took me by the hand, brought me to the apostles and told them my story for me.
It was around then that I spent fifteen days with Peter.
a06: Believers who had been scattered came to this city and told the Greeks about the Lord Jesus too.
Barnabas came all the way to Tarsus to find me and brought me here.
For a whole year we met with this church and taught.
a07: People from different homelands and families served the Lord together in this church.
One day, as they worshiped and fasted, the Holy Spirit called Barnabas and me.
The church laid hands on us and sent us off to the seaport.
a08: We crossed the sea, went across the island of Cyprus and reached this port city at its western end.
A wise governor wanted to hear the word, but a sorcerer at his side tried to stop him.
That day the hand of God was on that man, and the governor was amazed and believed.
a09: After crossing by ship to the mainland, we climbed a rugged mountain road and reached this city.
In the synagogue on the Sabbath they invited us to speak if we had a word of encouragement, so I stood up, motioned with my hand and spoke.
The next Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear the word.
a10: A man who had never walked since birth sat listening to me.
When he got up and walked, the crowd called us gods and brought oxen and garlands.
Not long after, the same crowd picked up stones, and I was dragged outside the city and left there.
a11: We won many disciples in this city. My hometown of Tarsus wasn't far.
But we turned back and went again into the cities where we had been driven out and stoned.
In each city we appointed elders and entrusted the disciples to the Lord.
a12: Some people came down to Antioch and taught the Gentile believers that they had to be circumcised.
The churches of Galatia were shaken too, so with astonishment and a heavy heart I wrote them a letter.
Because of that, Barnabas and I came up to this city to meet the apostles and elders.
a13: When I suggested visiting the churches we had started, Barnabas wanted to take Mark along.
I thought differently, and in the end we went our separate ways.
So I set out with Silas, who had come from Jerusalem.
a14: I came back to this very city where I had been stoned a few years before.
Here I met a young disciple the brothers all spoke well of.
In him was a sincere faith, passed down from his grandmother and his mother.
a15: When we tried to go into Asia, the Holy Spirit stopped us; when we tried to go to Bithynia, that road was closed too.
Turning this way and that, we came to this city by the sea.
That night I saw a man from across the sea calling me.
a16: We crossed the sea and came to this city — a leading city of Macedonia.
On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to the river, looking for a place of prayer, and found women gathered there.
One of them was baptized with her whole household and had us stay at her home.
a17: We were beaten and thrown into the inner prison, our feet fastened in wooden stocks.
At midnight Silas and I were praying and singing hymns, and the prisoners were listening.
Then the ground shook, and all the prison doors flew open.
a18: For three Sabbaths I explained the Scriptures in this city's synagogue.
When some came to believe, a jealous mob rushed to the house that had welcomed us.
That night the brothers secretly sent us off to Berea.
a19: While I waited for Silas and Timothy, I looked around this city and saw idols everywhere.
Every day I talked with people in the marketplace, until philosophers brought me to the council on the hill.
There I told them about the God who made heaven and earth.
a20: This is a great city on a narrow strip of land between two seas, crowded with ships and merchants.
I came into this city weak, fearful and trembling.
I met a couple just arrived from Italy, stayed in their home and made tents with them.
a21: My coworkers came down from Macedonia with good news about the church in Thessalonica.
When the opposition in the synagogue grew fierce, I moved right next door and kept teaching the word.
One night the Lord held me up in a vision.
a22: In this city I met about twelve disciples who had received only John's baptism.
For three months I spoke boldly in the synagogue, but some hardened their hearts and spoke evil of the Way.
So I took the disciples aside and taught them every day — for two years.
a23: In this city God did extraordinary things through my hands.
Then some men who imitated me, trying to drive out evil spirits, got a terrible fright.
The believers brought their costly books of magic and burned them in front of everyone.
a24: The craftsmen who made and sold silver models of the goddess's temple rose up in protest.
The whole city was in an uproar and rushed into the theater, shouting the same words for two hours.
I wanted to go out before the crowd, but the disciples held me back.
a25: It was after I had written a letter to the church in Corinth with great distress and many tears.
Even when we came here to Macedonia, there were fights outside and fears within.
Then the coworker I had been waiting for arrived and brought good news.
a26: I spent three winter months in this city.
I wrote a long letter to the believers in Rome, whom I had never yet visited.
In that letter I wrote of the road I dreamed of — the road all the way to Spain, at the ends of the earth.
a27: On the first day of the week, we gathered in an upstairs room in this city and broke bread together.
I was leaving the next day, so my talk went on until midnight.
A young man sitting in the window dozed off — and fell.
a28: To reach Jerusalem before Pentecost, we sailed past Ephesus and landed at this port.
I sent for the elders of the church in Ephesus and gave them my last words.
We all knelt and prayed, and they walked me to the ship, weeping.
a29: The disciples in Tyre knelt on the beach and prayed as they sent me off.
While I stayed at the house of Philip the evangelist in this city, a prophet came down from Judea.
Everyone wept and begged me not to go, but I was ready to go for the name of the Lord Jesus.
a30: I went up to the temple to complete the purification rites.
Some men from Asia recognized me and stirred up the whole crowd.
The temple gates were shut, and just as the beating began, soldiers came running.
a31: Carried by soldiers on the steps up to the fortress, I got a chance to speak to the commander.
When I motioned from the top of the steps, the angry crowd fell silent.
In Hebrew, I told them the story of the One I met on the Damascus road.
a32: When I stood before the Council, they split in two and argued over the resurrection.
That night the Lord stood beside me and said I must testify in Rome too.
At daybreak more than forty men swore not to eat until they had killed me.
a33: In the middle of the night, guarded by many soldiers, I was moved to this city by the sea.
The high priest even brought a lawyer down to accuse me before the governor.
I spent two years in prison in this city.
a34: A new governor came and asked if I would go up to Jerusalem to be tried.
I answered that I would stand before Caesar in Rome.
After that, I told the story of the light on the Damascus road again before King Agrippa.
a35: As a prisoner, I was handed over to the centurion Julius and boarded a ship bound for Rome.
It was the dangerous season for sailing, and I warned that the voyage would end in disaster, but no one listened.
Soon after we left Fair Havens, a terrible wind came rushing down from the island.
a36: For many days neither sun nor stars appeared. Everyone gave up hope of being saved.
That night an angel of God stood beside me and told me not to be afraid.
As day was dawning, I took bread in front of everyone and gave thanks to God.
a37: Swimming or holding on to planks from the broken ship, everyone made it onto this island.
It was rainy and cold, and the islanders built a fire and welcomed us.
As I put sticks on the fire, a viper came out and bit my hand.
a38: We spent the winter on the island, then reached Italy on a ship with the sign of the Twin Gods.
From Puteoli we walked toward Rome.
The brothers from Rome had come all the way to this forum to meet us.
a39: In Rome I lived in a rented house with a soldier guarding me.
From morning till evening I welcomed everyone who came and told them about the kingdom of God.
I was bound in chains, but the word was not bound.
a40: A slave who had run away from his master came to me while I was in chains.
He came to faith here, and I wanted to keep him by my side.
But I sent him back to his master, with a short letter written in my own hand.
a41: After I was set free from the rented house in Rome, I took to the road again.
I left one young coworker in Ephesus, and another here on this island.
I trusted him with the work still to be done, and set out on the road once more.
a42: Once again I was in chains in Rome. This time, my departure was near.
It was lonely. Only Luke was with me.
So I wrote to young Timothy: hurry and come before winter.
